narrativeReportMd:
# Library R4->R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No hard R4-valid-to-R6-invalid Library instance break was found in Library's own element model. The important migration risks are warning-level conformance tightening, optional R6-only metadata, one primitive type-domain shift, terminology binding changes, and semantic changes around canonical metadata such as jurisdiction and dependency references.

## Scope
The analysis used the local R4 and R6 core package StructureDefinitions and related terminology/datatype definitions. It excludes inherited base-resource changes and datatype-internal changes that should be owned by their own reports.

## Main migration themes
R6 adds canonical-resource metadata (`versionAlgorithm[x]` and `copyrightLabel`) that R4 cannot carry without extensions. `usage` changes from `string` to `markdown`, which is wire-compatible for normal JSON strings but changes generated types and primitive metadata. Terminology bindings for `subject[x]`, `type`, and `jurisdiction` changed, and `jurisdiction` also changed meaning from intended use jurisdiction toward maintaining-authority jurisdiction.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact local risks are semantic/conformance risks rather than hard validation failures: `Library.jurisdiction` has a changed meaning, `Library.subject[x]` moved to a different participant value set/system, and `Library.relatedArtifact` now warns when dependency/component relationships do not point to a resource.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most useful for terminology-dependent findings because the R6 core package did not include resolvable local definitions for some external terminology.hl7.org value sets, and no official ConceptMaps were supplied.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Most changes were implemented as optional additions, extensible bindings, or warning constraints, which reduces hard instance breakage. R4 round-trip support still needs extensions or policy decisions for new R6-only elements and for changed semantic interpretation.

## Follow-up analysis
Review the RelatedArtifact datatype report for child-level breaks under `Library.relatedArtifact`, and review external terminology packages or expansions for the moved library-type and jurisdiction bindings.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: Library keeps its identity and has no local required-element, removed-element, or reference-target break. The top concerns are R6-only metadata (`versionAlgorithm[x]`, `copyrightLabel`), changed terminology/semantics for `subject[x]` and `jurisdiction`, and new warning constraints on canonical URLs and dependency/component related artifacts. Confidence is medium because several terminology changes require external expansions or official migration notes.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is mostly about metadata interpretation and round-trip policy. R4-to-R6 import can preserve most existing Library content, but validators may emit new warnings and downstream business logic should revisit jurisdiction, topic, experimental, and dependency semantics. R6-to-R4 export needs extensions or loss-acceptance for R6-only optional fields and may need ConceptMaps or local rules for terminology binding changes.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural facts directly present in the two StructureDefinitions: no local element removals, no existing cardinality changes, new optional elements, and direct type/binding/constraint deltas. Confidence is lower for terminology impact because expansions were not performed and the R6 package points some bindings to external terminology.hl7.org value sets absent from the local package.

findings.title: R6 adds Library.versionAlgorithm[x] for version comparison

oldState.summary: No Library.versionAlgorithm[x] element existed in R4.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 Library had `version` but no computable element that declares how versions should be ordered.

newState.summary: Optional 0..1 choice element added with string and Coding choices.

semanticText.definition: Indicates the mechanism used to compare versions to determine which is more current.
semanticText.comment: If set as a string, this is a FHIRPath expression using %version1 and %version2.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 Library can declare a version ordering algorithm either as a string FHIRPath expression or a Coding from the version-algorithm value set.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Adding an optional element does not make an R4 Library invalid when read as R6. The break is in the reverse direction: an R6 Library that uses `versionAlgorithmString` or `versionAlgorithmCoding` cannot be represented as a native R4 Library element and will be rejected by strict R4 parsers unless transformed to an extension or dropped.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dropping version ordering metadata can change which Library version a resolver treats as current, but the effect is operational rather than a direct clinical data loss.

justification.inferredGoal: Make version ordering explicit for canonical resource resolution.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: this is an optional R6-only addition, not an R4-to-R6 base-shape break.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of making canonical version ordering explicit is reasonable, and the base R6 design does not invalidate existing R4 `Library` instances because `versionAlgorithm[x]` is optional. The compatibility issue is reverse-direction round-tripping into R4, so extension or drop policies are mitigations rather than evidence of a backward-compatible base-design alternative.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Under the calibration rules, additive optional R6 content is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue. Modeling the value only as an extension would improve R6-to-R4 round-trip behavior but would make the version-ordering signal less discoverable and less uniformly supported by native R6 tooling.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base design is needed; extension/backport handling is an R6-to-R4 migration concern.

evidence.detail: No R4 element with this id exists.
R6 adds optional 0..1 versionAlgorithm[x] with string and Coding types and an extensible version-algorithm binding.
evidence.quote: Indicates the mechanism used to compare versions to determine which is more current.

examples.examplesMd: The fragments are illustrative and show only the added R6 element and one possible extension-style export strategy; the exact cross-version extension URL should be confirmed against official conversion guidance.

findings.narrativeMd: `Library.versionAlgorithm[x]` is new in R6. Existing R4 Libraries can be read without it, but R6 producers can now send version ordering information that has no native R4 slot. This matters for package registries, canonical resolvers, and code that decides which Library version is newer.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation is not broken because the element is optional. R6-to-R4 conversion is lossy unless the algorithm is represented in an extension or out-of-band metadata. Strict R4 JSON parsers will reject `versionAlgorithmString` or `versionAlgorithmCoding` as unknown properties.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, leave the element absent unless a reliable version comparison policy is known. For R6-to-R4, preserve the value in a cross-version extension where possible and add tests for canonical resolution cases that depend on semantic version ordering.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change was made in the least disruptive base-shape form because it is optional. A pure extension would have been more backward-compatible for R4 but less useful to R6 tooling that needs a standard version-ordering element.

findings.title: R6 adds Library.copyrightLabel as a short copyright display string

oldState.summary: R4 had only Library.copyright for copyright and usage restrictions.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 Library modeled copyright information as a single optional markdown `copyright` element.

semanticText.definition: A short string (<50 characters), suitable for inclusion in a page footer that identifies the copyright holder, effective period, and optionally whether rights are restricted.
semanticText.comment: The copyright symbol and the '(c)' textual representation SHOULD NOT be included in this string.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 separates a concise rendered label from the longer markdown copyright statement.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is an optional R6-only element, so R4 data remains structurally valid in R6. The reverse conversion can lose a display/legal label unless it is copied into `copyright` or preserved as an extension.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Loss of the label can affect rendered copyright notices and compliance displays, but the full copyright markdown can still carry detailed restrictions.

justification.inferredGoal: Provide a concise copyright label for rendered artifacts while keeping full copyright details separate.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: this is an optional R6-only display/legal metadata addition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating a concise copyright label from full copyright markdown is a reasonable R6 goal and the element is optional. It therefore does not create a base R4-to-R6 validation break; the remaining issue is how to export R6-only content to R4 without losing the display label.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible base-design alternative is applicable for R4-to-R6 compatibility because old instances remain valid. A cross-version extension or convention in `copyright` is a migration/backport strategy, not a less-breaking R6 base design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4-to-R6 instances are preserved; R6-to-R4 preservation requires extension use or merging into existing copyright text.

evidence.detail: No R4 element with this id exists.
R6 adds optional string copyrightLabel.
evidence.quote: A short string (<50 characters), suitable for inclusion in a page footer

examples.examplesMd: An R4 Library cannot carry `copyrightLabel` as a native element. A migration can either merge it into `copyright` or use an extension.

findings.narrativeMd: `Library.copyrightLabel` is a new R6 convenience/legal-display field. It does not affect old R4 instances, but R6 content that relies on it has a round-trip problem when exported to R4.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 is unaffected. R6-to-R4 strict validation rejects the unknown `copyrightLabel` property. If dropped, rendered pages may lose the concise copyright holder/year statement even if the longer `copyright` element remains.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When producing R6, populate `copyrightLabel` only when a concise display label is known. When exporting to R4, preserve it in an extension or incorporate it into `copyright` with a clear delimiter so it can be reconstructed if needed.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The optional addition is mostly backward-compatible. A non-breaking alternative would have been a standard extension; that would reduce parser churn but would not give R6 renderers a uniform native location.

findings.title: Library.usage changes primitive type from string to markdown

semanticText.short: Describes the clinical usage of the library
semanticText.definition: A detailed description of how the library is used from a clinical perspective.

oldState.narrativeMd: The element was a primitive `string`; generated models commonly expose that as a string/string-type property.

semanticText.short: Describes the clinical usage of the library
semanticText.definition: A detailed description of how the library is used from a clinical perspective.

newState.narrativeMd: The element keeps the same name and cardinality but now declares the primitive type `markdown`.

facts.note: The wire property name and JSON scalar form are unchanged for ordinary primitive values.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Normal R4 JSON string values remain representable as R6 markdown strings, so this is not a direct instance-shape break. The risk is in generated code, schema validators, primitive metadata, and clients that distinguish `string` from `markdown` for rendering, sanitization, or length rules.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The element is descriptive metadata. Misrendering or sanitization differences are possible, but no direct clinical decision semantics were identified.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow formatted clinical usage guidance rather than only plain text.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `usage` as `string` and allow markdown by convention, or add a separate optional markdown element while retaining `usage`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of allowing formatted usage guidance is reasonable. Changing `usage` from `string` to `markdown` is not a normal JSON instance-shape break, but it can affect generated models and rendering/sanitization logic. Less-breaking designs exist, but they either fail to give R6 tooling a reliable markdown type or split one semantic fact across two fields, so the breakage appears probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained `Library.usage` as `string` with clarified text saying markdown may appear, preserving existing generated APIs. Another option would add `usageMarkdown` and leave `usage` untouched. The first alternative is incomplete because consumers still cannot know from the type that markdown rendering is intended; the second creates duplicate same-resource representations that may never converge.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The convention-only path weakens computable rendering semantics; a second field duplicates the same prose and risks divergence.

evidence.detail: R4 type is string.
R6 type is markdown.

evidence.locator: StructureDefinition-string and StructureDefinition-markdown primitive value regexes
evidence.detail: Both primitive types serialize as JSON strings for simple values in the supplied definitions.

migrationExampleJson.usage: Use this library for annual preventive care recommendations. See **Contraindications** before applying logic.

examples.examplesMd: The same JSON property can carry either plain text or markdown. Generated classes and renderers, not the JSON property name, are the main compatibility surface.

findings.narrativeMd: `Library.usage` keeps the same path and cardinality but changes from `string` to `markdown`. This is unlikely to invalidate ordinary instance JSON, but it can break compile-time APIs and change rendering/sanitization behavior.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with a normal non-empty `usage` string should remain valid in R6 because markdown is also represented as a string. R6 markdown content can usually be represented in R4 as a string, but systems may lose the typed signal that markdown rendering is intended. Strict code generators may expose different primitive wrapper types.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Regenerate models and review any code that treats `usage` as plain text. Rendering paths should apply markdown-safe rendering/sanitization in R6. Cross-version transforms can usually copy the scalar value directly, while preserving primitive extensions on `_usage` as usual.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A fully backward-compatible design could have added a new markdown-specific element and left `usage` as `string`, but that would duplicate content and complicate consumers. The chosen change is semantically cleaner but has codegen impact.

findings.title: Library.subject[x] binding changes from subject-type/resource-types to participant-resource-types/fhir-types

binding.description: The possible types of subjects for a library (E.g. Patient, Practitioner, Organization, Location, etc.).

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R4 value set compose explicitly includes Patient, Practitioner, Organization, Location, and Device from `http://hl7.org/fhir/resource-types`.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used a small value set of resource-type codes for coded Library subjects.

binding.description: The possible types of subjects for a library (E.g. Patient, Practitioner, Organization, Location, etc.).

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 compose explicitly includes ten participant resource type codes from `http://hl7.org/fhir/fhir-types`, including the five R4 code names but under a different system plus additional participant types.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 broadens coded subjects and changes the code system used by the preferred/extensible value set.

facts.note: The Reference choice target did not change; only the CodeableConcept binding changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The binding remains extensible, so non-member codes are not a hard validation error in the base resource. However, validators and terminology-aware applications may warn on R4 `resource-types` codings in R6, and R6 can express participant types that were not in the R4 subject-type value set.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Subject classification affects discovery, filtering, and applicability of knowledge artifacts. Incorrect or unconverted codings can make Libraries harder to find or apply.

justification.inferredGoal: Align coded subjects with a broader participant-resource type value set.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Include old `resource-types` subject codings in the R6 value set during transition while adding the new `fhir-types` participant codings.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Broadening coded subjects to participant resource types is a reasonable goal, and the extensible binding avoids a hard base validation failure. A less-breaking value-set design could have accepted the old R4 codings too, but that would preserve two systems for the same common concepts and complicate terminology validation and search normalization.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best base-design alternative is not merely a ConceptMap, which is migration guidance, but an R6 value set that explicitly includes both the old `http://hl7.org/fhir/resource-types` codings and the new `http://hl7.org/fhir/fhir-types` participant codings. That would preserve more R4 terminology validation behavior, but it has material long-term costs because old and new codings for Patient, Practitioner, Organization, Location, and Device could coexist indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Accepting both systems reduces warnings but prolongs duplicate codings for the same participant concepts and leaves terminology equivalence ambiguous.

evidence.detail: R4 binding is extensible to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/subject-type.
R6 binding is extensible to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/participant-resource-types.
R4 compose includes five resource-types codes; R6 compose includes ten fhir-types participant codes.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 example is still structurally valid in R6 but may not satisfy the R6 extensible binding because the coding system changed. The R6 example is structurally representable in R4 as CodeableConcept but falls outside the old R4 subject-type value set.

findings.narrativeMd: `Library.subject[x]` did not change cardinality or choice types, and the Reference target remains Group. The coded subject binding changed to a broader participant-resource-types value set using `fhir-types`, which can surprise systems that key on the old `resource-types` system.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: There is no hard base validation break because the binding is extensible. Terminology-aware validation can produce new warnings for old codings or for R6 participant codes when converting back to R4. Search/filter logic that compares coding system+code pairs must be updated.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map old `http://hl7.org/fhir/resource-types` subject codings to equivalent `http://hl7.org/fhir/fhir-types` codings where possible. Add local rules for new R6 participant types when exporting to R4, such as preserving both codings or accepting R4 extensible-binding warnings.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could have been less disruptive by including both value sets or providing a normative ConceptMap. The broader participant set is useful, but without a ConceptMap implementers must infer code-system migration rules.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: A terminology server expansion and official ConceptMap would improve confidence in whether any R4 codes are intended to be treated as equivalent to R6 fhir-types codes.

findings.title: Library.type extensible binding canonical moves to terminology.hl7.org

oldState.summary: Required Library.type element with extensible binding to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/library-type.

binding.description: The type of knowledge asset this library contains.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local R4 ValueSet includes the CodeSystem `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/library-type`, whose local codes are logic-library, model-definition, asset-collection, and module-definition.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 had a core-package value set canonical for library type.

newState.summary: Required Library.type element with extensible binding to http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/library-type.

binding.description: The type of knowledge artifact this library contains.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 StructureDefinition points to a terminology.hl7.org ValueSet that was not present as a local ValueSet JSON in the supplied R6 core package; the R6 short text adds `| etc.`, suggesting possible expansion beyond the four R4 examples.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 moves the binding canonical out of the FHIR core value set namespace.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The element remains mandatory with the same CodeableConcept shape and an extensible binding, so this is not a hard instance-shape break. The binding canonical change can affect terminology resolution, validator configuration, generated enum helpers, and code that recognizes the old value set URL.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: `Library.type` is required on every Library, so binding-resolution issues are likely to surface broadly, but the binding is extensible and generally affects classification rather than direct clinical content.

justification.inferredGoal: Move terminology ownership for library types to terminology.hl7.org and potentially broaden the value set.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the old value set canonical in the binding while moving stewardship/package ownership to terminology.hl7.org.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Centralizing terminology stewardship is reasonable, but the supplied local inputs do not show that changing the binding canonical URL was necessary to achieve it. Because `Library.type` is required on every Library and the R6 value set was not present locally, changing the canonical can disrupt terminology resolution and generated metadata even when instance codings are unchanged.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking R6 base design could have continued binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/library-type` while publishing or maintaining that value set from the terminology package. That would satisfy the stewardship goal with low to moderate tradeoff. A ConceptMap or ordinary migration note alone would not be enough; the less-breaking point is that the base binding URL itself could have remained stable.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves cached validators and generated binding metadata, at the cost of less uniform terminology.hl7.org URL naming and alias management.

evidence.detail: R4 binding valueSet is http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/library-type.
R6 binding valueSet is http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/library-type.

evidence.locator: R6 package index and glob search for library-type value set
evidence.detail: No local R6 ValueSet-library-type JSON was found in the supplied R6 core package.

examples.examplesMd: Existing instances using CodeableConcept codings remain structurally valid. The compatibility risk is mainly terminology validation and code that binds enum helpers to a specific value set canonical.

findings.narrativeMd: `Library.type` stays required and structurally unchanged, but its extensible binding moved from a core FHIR value set URL to a terminology.hl7.org URL. This can be a runtime/conformance issue even when the coded value is unchanged.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Base validation still requires `Library.type` but does not require all codings to be from the value set because the binding is extensible. Terminology validation may fail or warn if the R6 terminology package is unavailable or if applications only recognize the old value set canonical.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update terminology caches and generated binding metadata to resolve `http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/library-type`. Keep existing library-type CodeSystem codings where valid, but test validators with both R4 and R6 terminology packages.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The binding could have been migrated more compatibly by publishing an explicit alias or ConceptMap and including the old value set in the new one. Without those inputs, implementers should not assume exact expansion equivalence.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Requires review with an external terminology package or expansion service because the R6 value set was not in the supplied core package.

findings.title: Library.jurisdiction meaning changes from intended-use jurisdiction to maintaining-authority jurisdiction

oldState.summary: R4 jurisdiction described where the Library is intended to be used.

binding.description: Countries and regions within which this artifact is targeted for use.

semanticText.definition: A legal or geographic region in which the library is intended to be used.
semanticText.comment: It may be possible for the library to be used in jurisdictions other than those for which it was originally designed or intended.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 applications could reasonably use `Library.jurisdiction` as an intended-use or applicability filter.

newState.summary: R6 jurisdiction describes the authority that maintains the Library and encourages useContext for jurisdiction of use.

binding.description: Countries and regions within which this artifact is targeted for use.

semanticText.short: Jurisdiction of the authority that maintains the library (if applicable)
semanticText.definition: A legal or geographic region in which the authority that maintains the resource is operating. In general, the jurisdiction is also found in the useContext.
semanticText.comment: DEPRECATION NOTE: For consistency, implementations are encouraged to migrate to using the new 'jurisdiction' code in the useContext element.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 narrows the direct element toward maintainer jurisdiction and redirects intended-use jurisdiction to `useContext`.

facts.oldValue: A legal or geographic region in which the library is intended to be used.
facts.newValue: A legal or geographic region in which the authority that maintains the resource is operating.
Use useContext with usage-context-type#jurisdiction for jurisdiction of use.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The cardinality and type are unchanged, so instances do not fail structurally. The meaning changed enough that blindly copying R4 values into R6 can cause semantic misclassification: an R4 intended-use jurisdiction may be interpreted as the maintaining authority's jurisdiction.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Jurisdiction can drive artifact discovery, regulatory filtering, and applicability decisions. Misinterpreting intended use as maintainer authority can expose or hide Libraries in the wrong context.

justification.inferredGoal: Harmonize canonical resource metadata by using useContext for use jurisdiction and reserving jurisdiction for the maintaining authority.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `jurisdiction` as intended-use jurisdiction and add a distinct maintainer-jurisdiction element or additive useContext guidance.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of distinguishing maintainer jurisdiction from jurisdiction of use is reasonable, but changing the meaning of the existing `jurisdiction` element creates a semantic break for old data that remains structurally valid. A less-breaking base design could have preserved the R4 meaning and added the new maintainer concept explicitly, so this level of breakage appears probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest alternative is to leave `Library.jurisdiction` as the R4 intended-use jurisdiction and introduce a new field for the authority that maintains the Library, with optional guidance to also populate `useContext` for jurisdiction-of-use search. This retains a nonoptimal legacy shape but prevents silent semantic inversion. The tradeoff is another canonical metadata field and possible long-lived duplication if both direct jurisdiction and `useContext` are used for the same intended-use fact.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adds another metadata surface and may leave duplicate jurisdiction-of-use representations during transition, but avoids reinterpreting existing data.

evidence.detail: R4 defines jurisdiction as the region in which the library is intended to be used.
evidence.quote: A legal or geographic region in which the library is intended to be used.

evidence.detail: R6 defines jurisdiction as the authority that maintains the resource and includes a deprecation note directing use-jurisdiction to useContext.
evidence.quote: A legal or geographic region in which the authority that maintains the resource is operating.

evidence.detail: R6 binding valueSet changed to http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/jurisdiction.

examples.examplesMd: The example shows a possible R6 representation when an R4 jurisdiction value actually meant jurisdiction of use. Whether to also keep `Library.jurisdiction` depends on maintainer authority semantics.

findings.narrativeMd: `Library.jurisdiction` is one of the most important semantic changes. The same element path now emphasizes the jurisdiction of the maintaining authority, while intended jurisdiction of use should move to `useContext`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: There is no base structural validation break. The compatibility problem is semantic: old R4 values remain syntactically valid but may now mean something different. R6 values can be copied to R4 structurally, but R4 consumers may interpret them as intended-use jurisdictions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Classify each existing `jurisdiction` value as maintainer jurisdiction, intended-use jurisdiction, or both. For intended-use values, add a `useContext` entry with usage-context-type `jurisdiction`. Do not blindly duplicate values without confirming business meaning.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change could have been less ambiguous with a new element or a transition period where both meanings were explicit. Given the R6 deprecation note, migration guidance should be profile- or governance-specific.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 terminology.hl7.org jurisdiction value set was not available locally, so binding-content equivalence was not verified.

findings.title: R6 adds warning constraint that Library.url should not contain pipe, hash, or space

oldState.summary: No local Library.url warning constraint beyond normal uri validation.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 defined `url` as an optional canonical URI with no local invariant excluding `|`, `#`, or spaces.

newState.summary: R6 adds warning invariant cnl-1 on Library.url.

constraints.human: URL should not contain | or # - these characters make processing canonical references problematic

newState.narrativeMd: R6 warns when canonical URLs include characters that interfere with versioned canonical references and fragments.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The invariant is warning severity, so it should not make a conformant instance invalid by itself. It can still break pipelines that treat warnings as errors or that use URL strings containing `|`, `#`, or spaces in canonical resolution.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Canonical URL ambiguity can cause wrong-version resolution or failed dependency lookup, but the problematic characters should be uncommon in well-managed Library URLs.

justification.inferredGoal: Avoid canonical URL characters that conflict with version separators and fragment/reference processing.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the forbidden-character guidance as narrative text instead of a computable warning invariant.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Avoiding `|`, `#`, and spaces in canonical URLs is a reasonable interoperability goal, and R6 chose warning severity rather than an error. A narrative-only alternative would be less disruptive for warning-as-error pipelines, but it would not give validators a standard machine-checkable signal for a known canonical-resolution problem.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could have left this as prose or best-practice guidance outside the base invariant set. That alternative only partially meets the goal because problematic canonical URLs would be harder to detect consistently. The warning-level constraint is therefore a compatibility-conscious compromise rather than an avoidable hard break.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Narrative-only guidance avoids warning churn but is much less effective for automated canonical URL hygiene.

evidence.detail: No local R4 cnl-1 constraint is present on Library.url.
R6 adds warning constraint excluding pipe, hash, and space from Library.url.
evidence.quote: URL should not contain | or # - these characters make processing canonical references problematic

examples.examplesMd: This fragment illustrates an R4 Library URL that could become warning-producing in R6; the R6 constraint is warning severity rather than a hard invalidation.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a local canonical URL hygiene warning for `Library.url`. This mainly affects validation pipelines and canonical resolution, not basic JSON parsing.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 Library with a URL containing `#`, `|`, or a space can become R6 warning-producing. It is not a hard base validation break unless a server or CI policy escalates warnings to errors.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Scan Library canonical URLs for forbidden characters before R6 publication. If a URL contains a fragment or version separator, mint a clean canonical URL and handle old aliases through redirects, ConceptMaps, package metadata, or migration documentation.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The warning-level approach is reasonably backward-compatible. Making this an error would have been a hard break; keeping it only in prose would be less effective for tooling.

findings.title: R6 adds warning that dependency/component relatedArtifacts should reference a resource

oldState.summary: R4 Library.relatedArtifact had no Library-specific local invariant requiring dependency/component targets to be resources.

semanticText.comment: Each related artifact is either an attachment, or a reference to another resource, but not both.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed relatedArtifact entries using the RelatedArtifact datatype without a Library-specific dependency/component target warning.

newState.summary: R6 adds warning invariant lib-2 to Library.relatedArtifact.

constraints.expression: type in ('depends-on' | 'composed-of' | 'part-of') implies ((resource.exists() xor resourceReference.exists()) or (artifact is canonical xor artifact is Reference))
constraints.human: Dependencies and components of a Library should reference a resource

semanticText.comment: Each related artifact is either an attachment, or a reference to another resource, but not both. In addition, the successor or predecessor of a Library SHOULD be a Library, and dependencies and components of a Library SHOULD reference a resource.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 makes dependency and component relationships more computable by warning when they do not identify a resource.

facts.newValue: type in ('depends-on' | 'composed-of' | 'part-of') implies ((resource.exists() xor resourceReference.exists()) or (artifact is canonical xor artifact is Reference))

impact.impactRationaleMd: The new invariant is warning severity, not an error. It can still affect R4 Libraries that used `relatedArtifact` dependency/component relationships as free-text citations, documents, or unresolved URLs rather than resource references, because R6 tooling may rely on these targets for dependency resolution.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Library dependencies can affect CQL evaluation, data-requirements calculation, and package assembly. A missing computable dependency reference can lead to incomplete or incorrect executable artifact resolution.

justification.inferredGoal: Ensure Library dependencies and components are resolvable as resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Put the dependency/component resource-reference expectation in narrative guidance or a profile-specific warning instead of the base StructureDefinition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal is strong for Library: dependencies and components often need to be computably resolvable. Because the new invariant is warning-level, it does not make older content hard-invalid, while still making unresolved dependency modeling visible to tooling. Less-breaking alternatives exist but materially weaken the base interoperability signal.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking alternative would keep the expectation out of the base resource and express it in profiles, implementation guides, or prose. That would reduce validation churn for old descriptive related artifacts, but systems calculating dependencies would lose a common warning that applies broadly to Library rather than only to specialized profiles.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Profile-only or narrative guidance preserves quieter validation but weakens interoperable dependency resolution for executable Libraries.

evidence.detail: No R4 Library-specific lib-2 constraint is present.
R6 adds a warning invariant for depends-on, composed-of, and part-of relatedArtifacts.
evidence.quote: Dependencies and components of a Library should reference a resource

evidence.detail: R6 RelatedArtifact includes resourceReference and artifact[x] choices referenced by the Library-specific invariant; internal datatype changes are out of scope for this Library finding.

examples.examplesMd: An R4 Library with `relatedArtifact.type = depends-on` and only a citation or document can be structurally carried forward but will produce an R6 warning unless a resource/reference target is supplied. Exact child-property migration belongs to the RelatedArtifact datatype analysis.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a Library-specific warning that dependency, component, and part-of related artifacts should point to resources. This is not a hard instance break, but it is operationally meaningful for executable knowledge artifacts.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 Libraries that use descriptive related artifacts for dependencies may become warning-producing in R6. Runtime systems that compute dependencies may now expect `resource`, `resourceReference`, or `artifact[x]` target forms and may ignore or fail unresolved narrative-only dependencies.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit `relatedArtifact` entries with type `depends-on`, `composed-of`, or `part-of`. Where possible, populate a canonical or Reference target to the referenced Library, ValueSet, CodeSystem, PlanDefinition, or other resource. Treat purely narrative dependencies as requiring manual review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Warning severity is a reasonable backward-compatible compromise. The stricter expectation could have been profile-only, but Library dependency resolution is important enough that base-level warning guidance is useful.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Do not conflate this local Library warning with the broader RelatedArtifact datatype child-model changes, which should be assessed in the RelatedArtifact report.

findings.title: Library.name machine-identifier warning is tightened and renamed from lib-0 to cnl-0

oldState.summary: R4 root warning lib-0 checked Library.name against [A-Z]([A-Za-z0-9_]){0,254}.

constraints.human: Name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed a single-character uppercase name under the displayed regex and used a Library-specific invariant key.

newState.summary: R6 root warning cnl-0 checks name only when present and uses an anchored regex requiring at least two characters.

constraints.human: Name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation

newState.narrativeMd: R6 harmonizes the canonical-resource name warning and appears to require at least one character after the initial uppercase letter.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The invariant remains a warning, so it is not a hard validation break. It can produce new or differently keyed warnings for one-character names or names that relied on looser matching behavior.

justification.inferredGoal: Harmonize canonical-resource name rules for machine processing and code generation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Use the harmonized `cnl-0` warning with the old-compatible `{0,254}` length rule, or retain the old `lib-0` key during transition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Machine-usable names are a reasonable goal, but the R4 warning already addressed that goal and one-character uppercase identifiers can still be machine-usable. The evidence supports harmonizing wording or keys, but not clearly the tighter minimum length or the abrupt warning-key change for warning-sensitive tooling.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking R6 base design could have used `name.exists() implies name.matches('^[A-Z]([A-Za-z0-9_]){0,254}$')`, preserving the old allowed value set while adding anchoring and absent-name handling. If a shared `cnl-0` key was essential, a transition strategy retaining `lib-0` as an alias would also reduce breakage, though duplicate invariant keys can clutter suppression lists and may persist longer than intended.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves one-character names and warning suppressions; tradeoff is slightly weaker harmonization and possible temporary duplicate warning keys.

evidence.detail: R4 root warning uses lib-0 with regex [A-Z]([A-Za-z0-9_]){0,254}.
R6 root warning uses cnl-0 with name.exists() implies anchored regex {1,254}.

examples.examplesMd: A one-character name illustrates the warning change; this is warning-producing rather than hard-invalid in R6.

findings.narrativeMd: The machine-friendly `name` warning changed expression and key. The practical impact is mostly for validators, code generators, and CI systems that track invariant keys or fail on warnings.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No hard base validation break was identified. R4 Libraries with unusual or one-character names may receive different R6 warnings. Systems that suppress or assert specific invariant keys need to update from `lib-0` to `cnl-0`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Normalize Library names to start with uppercase ASCII and contain only letters, digits, and underscores, with at least two characters if following the R6 warning exactly. Update warning suppression lists and tests to use `cnl-0`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping this as warning-level is the main compatibility mitigation. A separate deprecation period for the old `lib-0` key would help warning-suppression tooling but would duplicate invariants.

findings.title: Library.experimental semantics are strengthened to mean no version will ever be for real use

oldState.summary: R4 experimental indicated the library was authored for testing purposes and not intended for genuine usage.

semanticText.short: For testing purposes, not real usage
semanticText.definition: A Boolean value to indicate that this library is authored for testing purposes (or education/evaluation/marketing) and is not intended to be used for genuine usage.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 conveyed non-production intent for the current Library.

newState.summary: R6 says no version of the resource will ever be intended for genuine usage and warns that experimental should not change across versions.

semanticText.short: For testing only - never for real usage
semanticText.definition: A Boolean value to indicate that this library is authored for testing purposes (or education/evaluation/marketing) and no version of this resource will ever be intended for genuine usage.
semanticText.comment: If experimental is 'true' for any version of a resource, it should be true for all versions of the resource.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 makes `experimental=true` a stronger lifecycle assertion across versions.

facts.oldValue: not intended to be used for genuine usage
facts.newValue: no version of this resource will ever be intended for genuine usage
If experimental is 'true' for any version of a resource, it should be true for all versions of the resource.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The boolean shape is unchanged, but lifecycle interpretation changes. A publisher that used `experimental=true` for early versions and later `false` for production release may be conformant to its R4 process but inconsistent with R6 guidance.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Production gating often depends on `experimental`. Misinterpreting a formerly experimental Library as permanently non-production can block valid content, while ignoring the flag can expose test logic.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify that experimental is an artifact identity/lifecycle property rather than a per-release maturity flag.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 current-artifact meaning and add a separate canonical-lifecycle signal or best-practice rule for permanent non-production artifacts.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Clarifying experimental status across versions is a reasonable governance goal, but the supplied evidence does not show that reinterpreting the existing boolean was necessary. The change can affect publication workflows that legitimately moved a Library from experimental to production under R4 semantics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking design could preserve `experimental` as the R4 version/current-artifact signal and add a distinct element, extension, or warning-level governance rule for resources that should never become production. That alternative is only partial because multiple lifecycle indicators can conflict, require coordinated tooling support, and make production filtering more complex.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids semantic reinterpretation but adds governance complexity and potentially two non-production indicators.

evidence.detail: R4 definition focuses on authored-for-testing and not genuine usage.
R6 definition says no version will ever be intended for genuine usage and comments that the flag should be true for all versions if true for any.

examples.examplesMd: No JSON shape example is needed because the boolean representation is unchanged. The migration issue is how governance interprets historical `experimental` values across Library versions.

findings.narrativeMd: `Library.experimental` did not change type or cardinality, but its definition became stronger. Systems that treat it as a temporary pre-production flag should revisit their publication workflow.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: No instance becomes structurally invalid. Runtime behavior may change in registries, package promotion workflows, or CDS engines that suppress experimental Libraries.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review version histories where a Library moved from experimental to production. In R6, consider minting a new canonical URL for production-ready artifacts if previous versions were truly experimental, or document local governance if retaining the same canonical.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This could have been introduced as narrative best-practice guidance rather than a stronger definition. Because there is no invariant, the practical break depends on governance and tooling policy.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This is a semantic/conformance finding, not a validator-enforced shape change.

R6 `Library.type` binds to this external terminology.hl7.org value set, but it was not present in the supplied R6 core package. Expansion or package resolution is needed to determine exact code-level compatibility with R4.
